key_insight: Fe or Cr substitution at Ni grain boundaries increases cohesion, with effects that depend on element type and local atomic structure.
engineering_relevance: Atomistically predicted separation energies and peak tractions could inform continuum fracture models for multicomponent Ni-based alloys.
method: Compute DFT rigid-body separation curves for six symmetric-tilt Ni grain boundaries.
Extract work of separation and maximum traction using the universal binding energy relation.
Benchmark ML interatomic foundation models against DFT, then sample finer alloy concentrations and a Ni56Fe20Cr24 composition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that one tested ML potential quantitatively reproduces DFT separation energies and peak tractions, enabling broader alloy-configuration sampling.
watch_item: Binary alloying trends do not quantitatively capture Fe–Cr interplay; explicit ternary calculations remain necessary.
paper_title: Alloying effects on the interface cohesion of grain boundaries in the Ni--Fe--Cr system
